Game theory
Computer software that models human behaviour can make forecasts, outsmart rivals and
transform negotiations
According to game theory, our chances of success in negotiations are based upon the
choices of others. Computer models have been developed to work out how events will
unfold as people and organisations act in what they perceive to be their own best
interests. Numerical values are placed on the goals, motivations and influence of ‘players’
and likely options are considered. Game theory software then evaluates the ability of each
of those players to influence others, and hence predicts the course of events.
Although many individuals would feel uncomfortable having a computer make decisions
for them, many organisations run such computer simulations for law firms, companies
and governments, But feeding software with accurate data on all the players involved ix
